name: Amoral

tenures.note: NPWA World Heavyweight Champion entering 1997 (won 24 Dec 1996 from Senator Carthy McJoseph); retained on PCW's own Birthday Brawl PPV (28 Jan 1997) and at Valentine's Day Massacre '97, had the belt physically stolen after the VDM match by Col. Jarrett, then lost it to Locutus (24 Feb 1997). Rebooked as a Triangle-match challenger at April Assault (11 Apr 1997) and again at Xmas Gory '97's Pinfall Royale, where he was the final entrant eliminated.

caption: NPWA World Heavyweight Champion entering 1997, who retained through January before Col. Buddy Lee Jarrett stole the belt outright after Valentine's Day Massacre and Locutus took the title from him days later.

name: Locutus

tenures.note: Won the NPWA World Heavyweight Championship from Amoral on Monday Night Mayhem (24 Feb 1997, Buffalo NY, top-rope 'Assimilator'); lost it (with Amoral reinstated in the interim) to Col. Buddy Lee Jarrett in a Triangle Match at April Assault (11 Apr 1997).

caption: Won the NPWA World Heavyweight Championship from Amoral in February 1997, losing it to Col. Buddy Lee Jarrett that April.

name: Col. Buddy Lee Jarrett

tenures.note: Won the NPWA World Heavyweight Championship in a Triangle Match over Amoral and Locutus at April Assault (11 Apr 1997); lost it to 'Superstar' Steve Sampson between April Assault and 20 May 1997 (the change itself is not directly attested; the fed's own printed champion list of 20 May 1997 already names Sampson). Also the NPWA's own first Television Champion (won a 16-man tournament, 16 Nov 1996) and founder of the New Wave of Wrestling stable.

caption: Won the NPWA World Heavyweight Championship in a Triangle Match over Amoral and Locutus at April Assault, already the promotion's first Television Champion and founder of the New Wave of Wrestling stable.

name: "Sadistic" Steve Stone

tenures.note: Won the inaugural NPWA North American Championship in a 15-man King of the Hill gauntlet at Valentine's Day Massacre '97 (14 Feb 1997); retained against Mark Bagwell at April Assault (11 Apr 1997); lost the title by 5 Jun 1997 to 'Breakfast' Bobby Toast. Also a former NPWA World Tag Team Champion (with A.T.M., 1995) and a New Wave of Wrestling stable member.

caption: Won a 15-man King of the Hill gauntlet to become the first NPWA North American Champion at Valentine's Day Massacre '97, retaining against Mark Bagwell at April Assault before losing the title that June.

name: Mustafa

tenures.note: Won the NPWA North American Championship by 22 Nov 1997; lost it to the Cougar at Xmas Gory '97 (24 Dec 1997). Also half of the Muslim Massacre, NPWA World Tag Team Champions (won 11 Apr 1997).

caption: Won the NPWA North American Championship in November 1997, losing it to the Cougar at Xmas Gory '97 that December, after an earlier reign as half of the Muslim Massacre's own NPWA World Tag Team Championship win that April.

name: The Cougar

tenures.note: Won the NPWA North American Championship from Mustafa at Xmas Gory '97 (24 Dec 1997), carrying it into 1998. A two-time former NPWA World Heavyweight Champion (1995) and, with the Coroner, the New Cadavre Connection tag champions (1996); won a 40-man Royal Rumble house-show special (2 Feb 1997, Sydney NS) as an inter-fed TNM World Title qualifier.

tenures.source: Competed in the reverse battle royal for the MLW Canadian Heritage Championship, 17 July 1999.

caption: Half of the Cadavre Connection's NPWA World Tag Team Championship reign from Xmas Gory '96 into April 1997, and NPWA North American Champion in his own right after beating Mustafa at Xmas Gory '97.

name: Jurisprudence

tenures.note: Won the NPWA Television Championship from the Southern Rocker (30 Jan 1997, Charlottetown PEI); lost it to the Mighty Boss on the April Assault pre-show (11 Apr 1997). Won a 16-man house-show tournament (9 Feb 1997, Mt. St. Pearl NF); a founding New Wave of Wrestling stable member.

caption: Won the NPWA Television Championship from the Southern Rocker in January 1997, a founding New Wave of Wrestling member, before losing the belt to the Mighty Boss that April.

name: The Mighty Boss

tenures.note: Won the NPWA Television Championship from Jurisprudence on the April Assault pre-show (11 Apr 1997); lost it by 1 Jun 1997 to 'Bad Boy' Mark Bagwell.

caption: A wrestler billed by NPWA NANET in the surviving 1997 Usenet record (1997).

name: The Silent Striker

tenures.note: Won the NPWA Television Championship from Brian Masters (22 Sep 1997); lost it to Dark Justice by 10 Dec 1997. Unsuccessfully challenged 'Breakfast' Bobby Toast for the North American Title at Armageddon '97; won a London Bridge Death Match over Ramesses II at April Assault.

tenures.source: A retired guest at ringside at the promotion's own Maplemania 2, posted 5 September 2001, who punched Shawn Viper.

caption: Won the NPWA World Television Championship from Blackheart Brian Masters on Monday Night Mayhem in Sydney, Australia, holding it until December 1997.

name: Dark Justice

tenures.note: Won the NPWA Television Championship by 10 Dec 1997, carrying it into 1998; defended it in a Death Row Match (win by hanging your opponent over the top rope) over 'Ultimate' Mike Mitchells at Xmas Gory '97.

caption: Won the NPWA Television Championship in a Death Row Match at Xmas Gory '97, carrying the title into 1998.

name: The Southern Rocker

tenures.note: Held the NPWA Television Championship entering 1997 (won 24 Dec 1996), lost it to Jurisprudence (30 Jan 1997); a former two-time World Heavyweight Champion (1995) and the fed's own 1996 Wrestler of the Year, its longest-reigning World Champion. Fired in early 1997 after assaulting NPWA President Billy Joe Tunney -- the year's largest roster departure.

caption: Won the NPWA World Television Championship from Col. Buddy Lee Jarrett at Xmas Gory '96, holding it into late January 1997.

name: Akira Sasaki

tenures.note: Half of the Asian Triad; named alongside Kenshin Nobunaga in an angle credit on the Inhuman '97 pre-show (1 Jun 1997) and won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship with Nobunaga in a Triangle Tag Match over the Lords of the Ring and the Hell Razors at Armageddon '97 (3 Aug 1997); entered the Xmas Gory '97 Pinfall Royale (24 Dec 1997).

caption: Half of the Asian Triad with Kenshin Nobunaga, the pair won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship in a Triangle Tag Match at Armageddon '97 before he entered that December's Xmas Gory Pinfall Royale.

name: Kenshin Nobunaga

tenures.note: Half of the Asian Triad; wrestled Ramesses II on Monday Night Mayhem (20 Jan 1997) and won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship with Akira Sasaki in a Triangle Tag Match over the Lords of the Ring and the Hell Razors at Armageddon '97 (3 Aug 1997); entered the Xmas Gory '97 Pinfall Royale (24 Dec 1997).

caption: Half of the Asian Triad, won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship with Akira Sasaki at Armageddon '97, losing it that September.

name: Gan Green

tenures.note: Half of The Perfect Role Models with Mr. Wrestling, a recurring tag team across the whole held corpus (Traction Zone and Thursday Night Thrashings episodes in Nov 1996, Saturday Night Nightmare, April Assault, Inhuman '97, Xmas Gory '97) and a two-time NANny Award winner referenced on air; won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship with the Maltese Falcon (by 18 Sep 1997), the title changing hands from the Asian Triad. Also fielded in Summer Games' golf event as a recurring comedy vignette across all four served days.

caption: One half of the Perfect Role Models with Mr. Wrestling and a two-time NANny Award winner, won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship with the Maltese Falcon in September 1997, losing it that October.

name: Mr. Wrestling

tenures.note: Half of The Perfect Role Models with Gan Green, a recurring tag team across the whole held corpus (Traction Zone and Thursday Night Thrashings episodes in Nov 1996, Saturday Night Nightmare, April Assault, Inhuman '97, Xmas Gory '97); the Valentine's Day Massacre '97 kayfabe-breaking comedy fall (already served) paired him against Gan Green.

caption: A wrestler billed by NPWA NANET in the surviving 1997 Usenet record (1996).

name: The Maltese Falcon

tenures.note: Debuted in a 20-minute time-limit draw against 'The Wrecker' Mick McGreggor at April Assault (11 Apr 1997); wrestled the Cougar at Armageddon '97 (3 Aug 1997); paired with Gan Green to win the NPWA World Tag Team Championship from the Asian Triad (by 18 Sep 1997); entered the Xmas Gory '97 Pinfall Royale (24 Dec 1997), repeatedly seen alongside Gan Green on that card.

caption: With Gan Green, won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship from the Asian Triad by disqualification on Thursday Night Thrashings -- a finish upheld on review -- before forfeiting the title about five weeks later.

name: Tyr the Nightmare

tenures.note: Won a 40-minute Falls Count Anywhere opener over El Corazon de Piedra at Valentine's Day Massacre '97 (already served); rematched him in the Mask vs Mask Street Fight on actual London streets at April Assault (11 Apr 1997), unmasking him as 'Reynoso Torres'; named directly by a heel's in-ring threat on the Xmas Gory '97 pre-show (24 Dec 1997).

caption: A wrestler billed by NPWA NANET in the surviving 1997 Usenet record (1997).

name: El Corazon de Piedra

tenures.note: Debuted in a squash match on The Traction Zone (4 Nov 1996); lost a 40-minute Falls Count Anywhere match to Tyr the Nightmare at Valentine's Day Massacre '97 (already served); unmasked as 'Reynoso Torres' after losing the Mask vs Mask Street Fight rematch to Tyr on actual London streets at April Assault (11 Apr 1997), believed dead since a 1992 Taipei Death Match.

caption: A wrestler billed by NPWA NANET in the surviving 1997 Usenet record (1996).

notes: A new Perfect Role Model, billed from Gotham City at 305 lbs, who stands in for an absent Gan Green against Dark Justice on 18 January 1998 and loses.
caption: A newly-recruited Perfect Role Model who lost his first NPWA match to Dark Justice before rising to hold the NPWA Cruiserweight Championship undefeated through October 1998.

tenures.source: /promotions/npwa-nanet/archive/npwa-mayhem-1998-01-18.html; billed the undefeated NPWA Cruiserweight Champion, criticized on-air for rarely defending the belt (Mayhem, 18 May 1998); retained the title against Doug Arnott with a Shooting Star Press (Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special, 13 October 1998).

name: The Glitter Boy
notes: An undefeated wrestler from Hilton Head, South Carolina, accompanied by valet The Glitter Girl, already appearing unminted in the wing's own already-served 10 December 1997 show notes against Amoral. Challenges Bowa the Snake Man for the Television Championship on 18 January 1998; the match is broken up by outside interference before any fall.
caption: An undefeated challenger for the NPWA Television Championship whose January 1998 title match ended without a fall.

notes: One half of the tag team The Siberian Express, accompanied to the ring by Alexander Gudonov; debuts with a win over 'Wyldside' on 12 January 1998.

name: "The Demon" Damien Lestat
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1997: #176, tagged NWLP, MPWA, AAPW; 1998: #124, tagged NPWA, IIWA. The poll billed this wrestler more than one way across its editions: also as ""Demon" Damien Lestat". Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Climbed the RSPWF Top 200 across two editions, from #176 in 1997 to #124 in 1998.

tenures.source: /promotions/npwa-nanet/archive/npwa-mayhem-1998-01-12.html; also a central rival to "The Wrecker" Mick McGreggor across Disaster Area (14 May 1998) and Mayhem (25 May 1998).
Won the promotion's own 23 February 1999 control-of-the-company main event by count-out, then won a buried-alive match on the 17 July 1999 pay-per-view.

name: Doc Toxic
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll, until a run as a North American Title challenger in the fed's own 1998 record. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1997: #107, tagged TCW; 1998: #61, tagged NPWA, TCW; 2000: #124, tagged PCW; 2004: #146, tagged MLW.
caption: Placed in four editions of the RSPWF Top 200 — #107 in 1997, #61 in 1998, #124 in 2000, #146 in 2004 — best at #61.

identity.note: The registry's own decorated-aka guard reads this name as a normalized substring match against toxic-wwa. Recorded distinct, not merged: the only record this entity has is a placing in the RSPWF Top 200, which gives a ring name and a federation tag and nothing else — no dates, no roster, no URL, so three of the collision doctrine's own four signals are simply absent and the no-merge default holds. Every held-promotion roster the ranked names were checked against came back with zero overlap. Reopenable the moment either side gains a record the other can be checked against.
Name collision only with a separately-attested 1997 wrestler under a different promotion; no shared evidence.

tenures.source: Referenced in a promo, Disaster Area, 14 May 1998; North American Title challenger against champion Rick Kilgore, ending by walkout with his manager Karachel, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special, 13 October 1998.
Competed in the double scaffold match for the vacant MLW World Heavyweight Championship, 17 July 1999.
Lost the Toxic-versus-Toxic match to his masked impostor at Maplemania 2, posted 5 September 2001.

name: Valtharius the Mad
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll, until a debut in the fed's own Mayhem broadcast of 25 May 1998. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1998: #63, tagged NPWA, TCW, SCRA, IIWF; 1999: #117, tagged MLW, NPWA; 2000: #45, tagged LVPWA.
caption: Placed in three editions of the RSPWF Top 200 — #63 in 1998, #117 in 1999, #45 in 2000 — best at #45.

tenures.source: Debuted as a monster heel, attacking "The Wrecker" Mick McGreggor's bodyguard, Mayhem, 25 May 1998; also recurs in this wing's own existing 1997 show notes.
Won the vacant MLW World Heavyweight Championship in a double scaffold match, 17 July 1999.
Special guest referee for the Maplemania 2 main event until he left with Tiang-Li, posted 5 September 2001.

identity.note: Name collision only with a separately-attested 1997 wrestler under a different promotion; no shared evidence.

name: "The Wrecker" Mick McGreggor
caption: The NPWA World Heavyweight Champion through mid-1998, a cocky Columbus, Ohio bruiser who won the Dying Breath Match over Steve Sampson at the wing's own Xmas Gory '97 (debuting the stable Cold Death) and defended the belt into the held record's 1998 window before dropping it to "Breakfast" Bobby Toast off-screen.

tenures.source: named as winner of a Dying Breath Match over Steve Sampson at Xmas Gory '97 (24 Dec 1997); billed champion, Disaster Area 14 May 1998; retained by disqualification over Steve Stone (interference by Damien Lestat), Mayhem 25 May 1998; lost the title off-screen before 6 Oct 1998 (coverage gap) to "Breakfast" Bobby Toast.

name: Jolt
caption: A young, hyperkinetic NPWA Television Champion who won his first defense of the belt on 29 Sep 1998 and was still champion two weeks later.

tenures.source: won his first Television Title defense against Mike Mitchells (unminted) with the Caffeine Crashdown, Mayhem 29 Sep 1998; retained against "Untouchable" Randy Gant, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998.

name: "Untouchable" Randy Gant
caption: A cigar-smoking, handcuff-wielding brawler who was the first NPWA Millennium Champion before losing the inaugural belt in a chaotic three-way glove match.

tenures.source: billed the reigning NPWA Millennium Champion entering Mayhem 29 Sep 1998; lost the title that same night in a Coal Miner's Glove triangle match against "Superstar" Steve Sampson and Rick Kilgore; challenged Jolt for the Television Title at Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special (13 Oct 1998, unsuccessful).

name: Rick Kilgore
caption: The NPWA North American Champion across the 1998 run, a Las Vegas brawler whose rivalry with the returning Chris Lake and running war with the Perfect Role Models framed several of the wing's autumn cards.

tenures.source: billed NPWA North American Champion, retaining against The Kaiser (Mayhem 29 Sep 1998, Ratings Buster); part of a three-way Coal Miner's Glove match for the Millennium Title the same night (did not win); retained against The Glitter Boy in a ladder match (Mayhem 6 Oct 1998); retained against Doc Toxic when Toxic walked out mid-pin (Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special, 13 Oct 1998).

identity.note: A same-named entity (rick-kilgore-wwa) is WWA's own head referee, a different role in a different, unrelated federation. No shared evidence -- held distinct under the no-auto-merge rule.

name: Blade
caption: Half of the Masters of Disaster alongside Jack Hammer, a former NPWA World Tag Team and North American Tag Team Champion managed by Tank.

tenures.source: billed a reigning NPWA World Tag Team Champion (with Jack Hammer) entering Mayhem 29 Sep 1998, losing the belts to the Outcast Rogues that night; won the newly-created North American Tag Team Championship (with Jack Hammer) from Assault and Battery at Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998, after a masked interloper knocked out Eddie Simpson for the pin.

identity.note: The bare name 'Blade' is carried by unrelated entities in at least ten other wings (giwf, faw, iwf, xuw, cswa, inwi, ngw, hwf, aowf, cwfpro), none sharing any evidence with this NPWA wrestler. Held distinct under the no-auto-merge rule.

name: Jack Hammer
caption: Half of the Masters of Disaster alongside Blade, a former NPWA World Tag Team and North American Tag Team Champion managed by Tank.

tenures.source: billed a reigning NPWA World Tag Team Champion (with Blade) entering Mayhem 29 Sep 1998, losing the belts to the Outcast Rogues that night; won the newly-created North American Tag Team Championship from Assault and Battery at Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998 (a masked interloper knocked out Eddie Simpson for the pin).

identity.note: The same billing exists in action-extreme-wrestling (jack-hammer-aew), an unrelated wing with no shared evidence. Held distinct under the no-auto-merge rule.

name: Arion
caption: Half of the Outcast Rogues alongside Shaz, Japanese tag wrestlers who won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship on 29 Sep 1998 and lost it two weeks later.

tenures.source: recurring across the held record from Disaster Area (14 May 1998) and Mayhem (18, 25 May 1998) as part of a six-man tag scene; won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship with Shaz from the Masters of Disaster, Mayhem 29 Sep 1998 (Arion pinning Jack Hammer's partner in a restarted match referenced via 6 Sep 1998 Armageddon V footage); lost the belts to the Asian Revolution, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998.

name: Shaz
caption: Half of the Outcast Rogues alongside Arion, Japanese tag wrestlers who won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship on 29 Sep 1998 and lost it two weeks later.

tenures.source: recurring across the held record from Disaster Area (14 May 1998) and Mayhem (18, 25 May 1998); won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship with Arion from the Masters of Disaster, Mayhem 29 Sep 1998; lost the belts to the Asian Revolution, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998.

name: Tank
caption: Cigar-chomping manager of the Masters of Disaster (Blade & Jack Hammer), barred from ringside for their North American Tag Team Championship match at Hell On Earth.

tenures.source: managed the Masters of Disaster through their World Tag Team Championship loss (Mayhem 29 Sep 1998) and their North American Tag Team win (Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998, from which NPWA President Tunney barred him ringside).

identity.note: The bare name 'Tank' is carried by unrelated entities in other wings (iwf, cwfpro), with no shared evidence. Held distinct under the no-auto-merge rule.

name: The Man They Call Nug
caption: A gargantuan bodyguard aligned with Mick McGreggor during his 1998 NPWA World Heavyweight Championship reign.

tenures.source: McGreggor's ringside bodyguard, beaten down alongside him by Damien Lestat and Valtharius the Mad during the World Title defense against Steve Stone, Mayhem 25 May 1998.

name: Doctor Death
caption: Half of The Cult alongside Father Armageddon (and, in the ring, Locutus), the first NPWA North American Tag Team Champions.

tenures.source: billed a reigning NPWA North American Tag Team Champion, retaining with Locutus over the Larson Brothers (Mayhem 6 Oct 1998); lost the belts, teaming again with Locutus, to Assault and Battery (Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special, 13 Oct 1998).

identity.note: The same billing exists in fwf-1992 (doctor-death-fwf-1992, active 1992-93, an unrelated wing), with no shared evidence. Held distinct under the no-auto-merge rule.

name: Father Armageddon
caption: Half of The Cult alongside Doctor Death, the first NPWA North American Tag Team Champions; sat as a guest commentator during the belts' successful defense.

tenures.source: billed a reigning NPWA North American Tag Team Champion (Mayhem 6 Oct 1998), sitting at ringside on commentary while Locutus wrestled in his place; the Cult (Locutus & Doctor Death) lost the belts to Assault and Battery, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998.

name: Eddie Simpson
caption: Half of Assault and Battery alongside Tom Harris, NPWA North American Tag Team Champions for under three weeks in October-November 1998.

tenures.source: won the NPWA North American Tag Team Championship with Tom Harris from The Cult (Locutus & Doctor Death), Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998; lost the belts to the Masters of Disaster at Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998, after a masked interloper knocked him out mid-match.

name: Tom Harris
caption: Half of Assault and Battery alongside Eddie Simpson, NPWA North American Tag Team Champions for under three weeks in October-November 1998.

tenures.source: won the NPWA North American Tag Team Championship with Eddie Simpson from The Cult (Locutus & Doctor Death), Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998; lost the belts to the Masters of Disaster at Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998.

name: "The Immovable Object" Jo Ozawa
caption: Half of the Asian Revolution alongside Takanori, teaming with "Breakfast" Bobby Toast to win the NPWA World Tag Team Championship from the Outcast Rogues.

tenures.source: named as a rival to the Outcast Rogues for the World Tag Team belts entering Mayhem 29 Sep 1998; won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship (with Takanori) by pinning the Glitter Boy in a Double Jeopardy six-man match, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998, then mockingly refused to hand the belts back to the Rogues; retained against the Rogues at Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998.

name: Takanori
caption: Half of the Asian Revolution alongside Jo Ozawa, teaming with "Breakfast" Bobby Toast to win the NPWA World Tag Team Championship from the Outcast Rogues.

tenures.source: named as a rival to the Outcast Rogues for the World Tag Team belts entering Mayhem 29 Sep 1998; won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship (with Jo Ozawa) at Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998; retained against the Rogues at Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998.

name: Baron Von Duttley

tenures.source: The NPWA No-Star Jobber Rumble (written July 1999, posted March 2001), whose commentary recalls his July 1997 match with Valtharius the Mad.
tenures.note: The fingerless Claw Master of Brampton, Ontario, one of the Duttley Clan; won the No-Star Jobber Rumble while unconscious for nearly the whole match, then goose-stepped around the ring.

caption: A fingerless Brampton jobber known as the Claw Master, who won the NPWA No-Star Jobber Rumble while unconscious for nearly the whole match.
